flash_693085.description:
Palestinian Arabs reported clashes with Israelis in the village of Hajjah, east of Qalqilya. According to their claims, a drone operating over the village was brought down after Palestinian Arabs threw rocks at it. The Israelis then arrived in the village to retrieve the drone, leading to clashes at the scene.

According to the reports, an Israeli military force that arrived at the scene opened fire at Palestinian Arabs who were throwing stones at the soldiers. The Palestinian Arabs reported that one person was killed in the incident.

A man in his 40s was moderately injured after being hit by a car while riding an electric scooter in Ashdod.

Magen David Adom (MDA) teams provided him with medical treatment and evacuated him to Sheba Hospital at Tel Hashomer.

flash_693131.description:
Yesterday (Sunday), the IDF struck in the Gaza City area and eliminated the terrorist Yusuf Aqila, a Nukhba company commander in Hamas’ military wing.

In recent weeks, the terrorist advanced attacks against IDF troops and Israeli civilians and worked to restore the terrorist organization's capabilities, in systematic violation of the ceasefire. The terrorist was eliminated to remove the threat he posed.

flash_693130.description:
Hatzibur HaCharedi announced today that it has informed the chairman of the Amcha Yisrael party that it will not accept the merger proposal presented to it. Party officials said the decision was based on current polling, which, in their assessment, does not provide sufficient confidence that the proposed arrangement would cross the electoral threshold, nor would it secure adequate representation for the haredi public and answer the needs of its voters.

“Hatzibur HaCharedi will not enter into an arrangement that fails to provide our voters with a credible path to parliamentary representation," party officials said.

The party added that it remains committed to securing representation in the next Knesset for the Charedi public who are not represented, and the party leadership will continue to evaluate all available political options to secure that representation.

flash_693129.description: Netanel Jacobs recounts from his hospital bed at Beilinson the struggle with the terrorist who stabbed him.

flash_693128.description: Finance Ministry data released ahead of Rosh Hashanah 5787 show growth in Israel’s economy despite years of war and uncertainty, with foreign investment surging 78%, inflation falling and the shekel strengthening.

flash_693127.description:
Earlier today (Monday), during IDF patrols in the Beaufort area in southern Lebanon, a Hezbollah terrorist inside a building opened fire at the soldiers.

The soldiers returned fire and eliminated the terrorist.

During the close-quarters encounter, two IDF soldiers were lightly injured and were evacuated to receive medical treatment. Their families have been notified.

Additionally, the IDF struck weapons storage facilities, command centers, and additional terrorist infrastructure belonging to the Hezbollah terrorist organization in the area.

flash_693126.description: Thai authorities have ordered the deportation of Kevin Dimino, director of a wildlife park on Koh Samui, after he placed a Palestinian flag and signs prohibiting the entry of Israelis.

Amcha Yisrael Party chairman Ofer Winter and the slate’s number two candidate, Yoseph Haddad, were filmed celebrating with baklava after submitting their Knesset slate.

They were also banned from attending soccer matches for 60 days.

flash_693150.description:
National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir responded to Britain's expected decision to impose sanctions on Judea and Samaria.

"The time has come for the State of Israel to publicly recognize the Falkland Islands as occupied Argentine territory, which the British are violently stealing from the Argentine people. The British are not only occupying the territory, but are also conducting oil drilling there and stealing money from the Argentine people," he said.

"I call on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to recognize Argentina's sovereignty over the Falkland Islands and impose sanctions on Great Britain for as long as the occupation continues," added Ben Gvir.

Three suspects were arrested in Lod on suspicion of involvement in the shooting of two people in the city this evening.

According to the police, the forces arrived at the scene shortly after receiving the report, began searching and located the three. They were taken in for questioning.

Al-Shaibani also said that Damascus opposes Iranian attacks against the Gulf states and Jordan and supports a diplomatic solution with Israel.

Britain intends to impose a trade ban on products manufactured in Judea and Samaria tomorrow (Tuesday), the New York Times reported.

Lebanese Foreign Minister Youssef Raggi accused the Hezbollah terrorist organization of dragging the country into two consecutive wars over the past two years, despite repeated warnings about the dangers involved and the expected harm to Lebanon’s security.

In an address to a meeting of Arab foreign ministers in Cairo, Raggi strongly condemned Israeli strikes and violations of Lebanese sovereignty, as well as Israel’s seizure of extensive areas in the country.

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham spoke with the Emir of Qatar about the situation in the Middle East, particularly in Gaza and Judea and Samaria.

Burnham’s office said he told the Emir that he was focused on securing calm and supporting regional partners in an effort to restore stability and security.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s associates are making a last-minute effort to bring about a merger between Avi Maoz’s Noam L'Yisrael party and Bezalel Smotrich’s Religious Zionist Party, Kan Reshet Bet reported on Tuesday morning.

No substantive talks are currently taking place between Maoz and Smotrich, but Netanyahu’s associates are trying to persuade both sides that a merger would serve their interests. They have warned that running independently could prompt Maoz to withdraw shortly before the elections and that Likud’s campaign would prevent his party from gaining support.

President Isaac Herzog addressed discussions in Britain and other countries about imposing sanctions, saying that if they are enacted, “it would constitute a grave error in judgment and a choice to stand on the wrong side of history."

Herzog added that such measures would amount to “blatant interference in democratic elections" and urged foreign governments: “Stop! Step back from the dead end of sanctions and boycotts."

flash_693212.description:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio was asked about the UK sanctions on Jewish communities in Judea and Samaria.

He stated: "They alerted us to it. We don't have any announcements. Obviously, those are decisions that they make, and we and the President have expressed this in the past. We don't want to see anything destabilizing going on right now in the West Bank with so much going on in the region. We think it has implications as well on our ability to make progress with regards to Gaza and the 20-point plan and the border peace that we're very committed to. Obviously, we're not going to do what the UK did. We saw their announcement today, but I don't have any comment on it right now."

flash_693210.description: More than 30 terrorists were arrested by the Shin Bet, IDF and police on suspicion of involvement in the terrorist infrastructure - some had been released in one of the hostage deals.

flash_693208.description:
Following the imposition of sanctions on Judea and Samaria, Israel decided to ban 12 British leaders and citizens from entering its territory.

Among the individuals whose entry will be banned is Jeremy Corbyn, former leader of the British Labor Party.

flash_693199.description: Former Prime Minister Yair Lapid has attacked the British government's decision to impose boycotts and sanctions on Israel. He said it is a "wrong and dangerous policy" that will strengthen extremist voices in Israel ahead of the elections and encourage Hamas and terrorist organizations. Lapid claimed that the decision stems from domestic political considerations in Britain.

Jordan announced that 20 ballistic missiles were launched from Iran toward its territory, with its air defense systems intercepting and destroying 18 of them.

According to the statement, the two remaining missiles landed in areas away from population centers. No casualties were reported in the attack.

Minister of Diaspora Affairs Amichai Chikli attacked the Ra'am party and its candidate Yoav Segalovitz on Tuesday evening.

“We are inches away from the Yamam receiving orders from the Shura Council. This is not a hand on the wheel; it is a hand on the trigger of the State of Israel," Minister Chikli said.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) confirmed that it launched missiles at a US military base in Jordan in response to US attacks on Iranian oil tankers.

At the same time, the IRGC announced plans to attack oil tankers in Kuwait and Bahrain and called on their crews to “abandon the ships."

The barrage was clearly visible from Israel, but did not cross into Israeli territory.

United Hatzalah teams arrived at Rabbi Shimon Agassi Street in Jerusalem's Har Nof neighborhood following a gas balloon explosion in a residential building.

Firefighters are operating at the scene, and a three-year-old girl sustained light injuries.

flash_693258.description: Police say new evidence reveals how the supermarket products were allegedly tampered with - but one major question remains unanswered.

flash_693254.description: Gaza report: Israeli UAV struck in western Rafah

flash_693252.description: After losing wife and two daughters to Palestinian terrorists, Rabbi Leo Dee challenges Andy Burnham over proposed boycott: 'I would be happy to debate you on television, anywhere and at any time.'

flash_693250.description: Jacob Coxon, an AI researcher who worked at both Anthropic and OpenAI, has left the industry while issuing a stark warning about the race toward superhuman artificial intelligence.

flash_693248.description: IDF strikes destroy three Hamas, Islamic Jihad, weapons depots packed with rockets and rifles, along with a launch pit used to fire at Israel throughout the war.

flash_693246.description:
The Trump administration reportedly did not oppose the British initiative to impose sanctions on the settlements in Judea and Samaria, and did not even act to block the move, according to Channel 12.

According to the report, the White House's decision not to act against the move, to which 12 Western countries have joined, may indicate frustration in the American administration with the policy of the Netanyahu government.

flash_693292.description: UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband rejects Chief Rabbi Ephraim Mirvis’ warning that sanctions on Judea and Samaria could fuel antisemitism in Britain.

flash_693291.description: Likud demands an investigation into the newspaper and three of its writers over allegations that senior PA official Mohammed Dahlan was involved in the publication of a false report.

flash_693290.description: Iranian reports of explosion in Jask on the Gulf of Oman

flash_693289.description: From Mount Hermon, Defense Minister Katz vows Israel will remain in the Syrian security zone and warns that Iran could face a third Israeli strike.

flash_693288.description:
Biden-era Secretary of State Antony Blinken denied a Haaretz report that Qatar conveyed a Hamas offer to return the hostage immediately after the October 7th massacre and that he rejected it.

"For the record, this is false. Complete fiction," Blinken stated.

flash_693287.description:
Israeli Foreign Minister Giden Sa'ar spoke on Wednesday with Reform UK leader Nigel Farage following the anti-Israel moves by the Labour Government.

Sa'ar thanked Farage for his and his party’s support for Israel. Farage shared that he was pleased to have addressed the Reform Friends of Israel event at the party conference in Birmingham last week.

The British politician also assured Sa'ar that, in government, Reform UK would reverse the damage done to the UK-Israel relationship by the Labour Government and its policies.

flash_693286.description: Dr. Shmuel Katz urges Israelis abroad to participate in the elections and calls on smaller right-wing parties to unite, warning that votes for parties that fail to cross the electoral threshold could ultimately weaken the right.

flash_693285.description: Former NYC Mayor Eric Adams joins Israeli energy company TurboGen’s Advisory Board, helping drive US expansion and new opportunities for its power technology.

flash_693284.description: IRGC says war with the US could end if Washington meets Tehran’s demands on frozen assets, nuclear and missile programs, Yemen and Lebanon.

flash_693283.description: Jewish leaders warn the measures targeting Israeli businesses in Judea and Samaria will isolate Israel, undermine cooperation and hinder peace efforts.

flash_693282.description: The father of captivity survivor Eitan Mor and Religious Zionism Knesset candidate sharply attacks British sanctions on Jewish communities in Judea and Samaria.

flash_693281.description: Tzipi Hotovely, head of Israel’s National Public Diplomacy Directorate, told Channel 12 News that following the boycott targeting Jewish communities in Judea and Samaria, “our intelligence cooperation with Britain will be reduced."

flash_693280.description: Israel Police spokesman Dean Elsdunne speaks to Arutz Sheva about October 7, the battle for Israel’s truth abroad, and why Israelis must keep speaking out.

flash_693279.description: Why all the other signatories of Foreign Secretary Miliband’s antisemitic initiative weren’t also sanctioned by having their consulates in Jerusalem closed is totally beyond me.

flash_693278.description: Answers to the question posed by the Mussar master, Rav Israel Salanter.

flash_693277.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu visited the Mount Hermon summit with the defense minister. “The main task is to defeat the terror regime in Iran. We are close to achieving that."

flash_693276.description: An allegation from anonymous sources in a book released for maximum marketing sales is ugly stuff. Opinion.

flash_693272.description: The Sages decreed not to blow the shofar out of fear that a single Jew who does not know how to blow might carry his shofar on Shabbat in a public domain. For the sake of that single Jew, we suspend the mitzvah of shofar-blowing that year for all the people of Israel!

flash_693270.description: Nearly two years after fighting for his life, Itamar Galinsky returns to reserve duty in the same unit where he was wounded. 'The nation of Israel lives!'

flash_693268.description: Annual Rosh Hashanah pilgrimage sends rentals and businesses soaring as the Ukrainian city prepares for tens of thousands of visitors.

flash_693266.description: Rebbetzin Esther Jungreis, the sacred lessons of September 11, and a divine call to awaken. Op-ed.

flash_693263.description: On the morning of September 11, 2001, Danny Lewin boarded American Airlines Flight No. 11 in Boston, expecting to reach Los Angeles. In the course of a struggle that took place between Lewin, a graduate of Israel’s elite commando unit, Sayeret Matkal, and the four hijackers who were assaulting the cockpit, Lewin was murdered by armed Satam Al Suqami, a 25-year-old Saudi.

flash_693298.description: Reports of Israeli strikes in several areas of southern Lebanon

flash_693297.description: President Trump predicts the Iran war will end after November’s midterms, accusing Tehran of trying to influence the vote and warning of more US strikes.

flash_693295.description:
President Donald Trump told the press that he believes that the war with Iran will end immediately after the midterm election.

He explained: "They can't hold out any longer. They're desperate to try and affect the election so that we could get a nice, weak group of people in there and leave them alone and let them have their nuclear weapon."

flash_693294.description: IAEA Board refers Iran to the UN Security Council for the first time in 20 years over Tehran’s failure to cooperate with a probe into undeclared uranium.

flash_693293.description: Channel 14 poll shows the right-wing bloc winning 64 seats, compared to 44 for the anti-Netanyahu bloc.

flash_693309.description:
The Democratic Reform Current of Fatah, headed by Mohammed Dahlan, attacked Likud following the party's accusations that Dahlan was behind a report in Haaretz claiming that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ignored a warning received from the United Arab Emirates before October 7.

“We are following the incitement campaign being led by Benjamin Netanyahu and the Likud party against leader Mohammed Dahlan, in a blatant attempt to drag his name into Israel's election campaign and evade the difficult questions Netanyahu is facing inside Israel regarding his political responsibility for the failures of October 7."

It added: “The allegations raised by Likud against Mohammed Dahlan, and the claims that he is interfering in Israel's elections, are nothing more than absurd and misleading allegations. They expose the extent of the confusion and disorder within the Netanyahu camp - a camp that has become isolated on the international stage and tainted by the disgrace of genocide against our Palestinian people."

flash_693308.description: Actor John Malkovich cancels his planned Tel Aviv performance in 2027, claiming an Israeli PR firm falsely attributed quotes to him without his approval.

flash_693306.description: Iranian media report several areas in Sirik have been hit

flash_693304.description: Home Front Command: Incident in northern Israel has concluded

flash_693302.description: Sirens sounded along the northern border due to suspected UAV infiltration

flash_693300.description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio says Iran will face further consequences for attacks on US ships as Washington maintains economic pressure on Tehran.

flash_693296.description: Israel’s UN Ambassador Danny Danon launches international initiative with dozens of countries, calls for fight against antisemitism to be prioritized in selection of next UN chief.
